header:
Date: 2026-07-14
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Nandakumar (Redwood SE), Marcus Leung (VP Platform, Elytrex), Sofia Alvarez (SRE, Elytrex), Ibrahim Conteh (CTO, Elytrex)
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on recent benchmark runs comparing Redwood inference against the customer's incumbent provider. Reviewed p50/p95/p99 latency, sustained throughput (rps), and error/retry behavior. Discussed routing strategies (latency-first vs cost-first), prefix/KV caching impact, and next steps for a short A/B routing experiment and Dedicated slot reservation. Security and network hoops (SOC2, KMS, VPC peering) surfaced as gating items for Dedicated deployment.
topics: Bench numbers (p50/p95/p99), throughput vs concurrency, batching and cache effects, quantization profile impact, routing policy (latency vs cost), Dedicated capacity slot request, security/compliance checkpoints (SOC2/KMS/SSO), network/VPC peering checklist
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Ellis: Hey everyone thanks for making time, we'll run through the bench numbers first and then talk routing and the dedicated ask. Priya and I will chime in on tuning options.
[00:22] Marcus Leung: Thanks Jordan, excited to see the numbers. We've been feeling the latency spikes during peak windows so hoping there's a clear win.
[00:34] Priya Nandakumar: Hi all — quick note, we ran three runs last night: baseline (your incumbent), Redwood default hosted route, and Redwood with prefix/KV cache + quant profile. I'll try to summarize high level then drop links.
[00:48] Sofia Alvarez: Quick interjection — network was stable during our runs, we pinned the test clients to the eu-west region.
[00:55] Priya Nandakumar: OK so p50 numbers first: Incumbent p50 ~ 320ms; Redwood hosted p50 ~ 270ms; Redwood cached+quant p50 ~ 210ms. For p95: Incumbent ~ 1,120ms; Redwood hosted ~ 780ms; Redwood cached+quant ~ 540ms. p99 gaps are similar but noisy.
[01:20] Ibrahim Conteh: Nice, that p95 delta is meaningful. Are those end-to-end latencies including network and TLS?
[01:28] Priya Nandakumar: Yes end-to-end from the test client. We also collected server-side token timings — the main uplift came from reduced KV cache misses and smaller kernel paths with the quant profile.
[01:40] Marcus Leung: Throughput numbers? We need sustained rps for our batch jobs — target is 120 rps with 512 token avg.
[01:47] Priya Nandakumar: Sustained throughput at 512 tokens: Incumbent handled ~70 rps at target SLO before queueing; Redwood hosted steady-state ~95 rps; Redwood cached+quant peaked ~135 rps with tails trimmed. So with a dedicated slot you'd have headroom.
[02:05] Jordan Ellis: To be transparent — our hosted tests had slightly better latency variance than the incumbent but the routing fallbacks matter. If you want guaranteed headroom we recommended Dedicated capacity reservations.
[02:18] Marcus Leung: Yeah cost is a factor, dedicated is a commitment. Can you show what Reserved buys us in terms of p95/rps?
[02:26] Priya Nandakumar: We projected that a small Dedicated pool (2x A100-equivalent) would move p95 to ~380-420ms at 150 rps worst-case, and cached+quant dedicated to ~260-300ms p95. Those are conservative estimates — we'll run a Dedicated slot test if you want.
[02:42] Sofia Alvarez: What about warmup and KV cache cold start? We saw big spikes on the incumbent when the cache was cold.
[02:49] Priya Nandakumar: Good call. KV cache cold starts were the main cause of the incumbent p99 spikes. Our automatic warmup + continuous batching reduces cold miss rate, but during a big traffic ramp you can still get transient. We can pre-warm the cache for known prefixes for the pilot.
[03:05] Ibrahim Conteh: Can Redwood route by latency for production and fall back to cheaper variants? That's important so we can balance cost and latency during off-peak.
[03:13] Jordan Ellis: Yes — smart routing can be latency-first or cost-first. You can set thresholds: route to Dedicated if p95 > X, else use hosted cheaper variant. Also automatic fallback to smaller quant models.
[03:25] Marcus Leung: What about model fidelity — do we see accuracy loss with the quant profile? We care about hallucination and answer quality.
[03:32] Priya Nandakumar: We compared output on our eval set; small differences in fluency, no obvious regression on task accuracy for the prompts you gave us during onboarding. We can run your acceptance prompt set again and surface diffs.
[03:46] Sofia Alvarez: Security questions — KMS key usage, audit logs, SSO integration. Dedicated means keys are customer-managed?
[03:53] Jordan Ellis: For Private/Dedicated you can bring your own KMS/HSM, yes. We emit comprehensive audit logs (request/response metadata redacted by default) and support SAML/SSO via SCIM for provisioning. We'll share the SOC2 and network checklist.
[04:07] Ibrahim Conteh: Any gotchas for VPC peering? We run strict egress rules.
[04:12] Priya Nandakumar: We have a VPC peering guide. Usually needs a cidr allowance for peering endpoints and firewall rules for healthchecks. We'll work with your infra team. Sofia if you share the network contact we'll open a ticket.
[04:23] Marcus Leung: Ok nuts and bolts — what's the next step if we want to reserve a Dedicated slot for one week of testing?
[04:29] Jordan Ellis: We can provision a week-long Dedicated window, you pay the reserved rate pro-rated. We typically need a 72-hour lead to stand up everything including routing and KMS. If you want 7/20 window we should lock it in by 7/17.
[04:43] Sofia Alvarez: I'll check calendar and budget and get back to you.
[04:47] Priya Nandakumar: Technical note — we saw error retries from incumbent at scale (502/504). Redwood had lower retry rates in our runs. I can attach the error waterfall chart.
[04:57] Jordan Ellis: Also wanted to call out batching effects: increasing dynamic batching increased throughput but increased median latency slightly; with prefix cache on the tail improves drastically. There's a tradeoff knob there.
[05:10] Marcus Leung: Can you run an A/B where 50% traffic uses Redwood cached route and 50% incumbent for a 24h window? We'll need to show platform team the real world delta.
[05:19] Jordan Ellis: Yes, we can orchestrate split routing for the pilot. We'll need a routing policy and a runbook for how to flip traffic and monitor SLOs.
[05:28] Sofia Alvarez: We'll need to know what telemetry we'll get — token-level costs and trace IDs for correlating with our logs.
[05:34] Priya Nandakumar: You get token-level cost and per-request trace IDs and the per-model latencies. We can also emit trace hooks to your tracing provider.
[05:42] Ibrahim Conteh: On the quantization profile, is the model variant deterministic? We worry about nondeterminism affecting downstream scoring.
[05:49] Priya Nandakumar: Determinism is mostly invariant but there are small differences due to kernel scheduling; if you require byte-for-byte determinism we can pin to the same model weights and disable non-deterministic kernels, but that impacts performance.
[06:05] Marcus Leung: All right, from business side I want to see the exact cost delta for the Dedicated week vs paying hosted over a month. Jordan can you provide a pro-forma?
[06:12] Jordan Ellis: Yes I'll send a simple cost model that compares per-token hosted run vs pro-rated Dedicated slot with the headroom numbers we discussed.
[06:18] Sofia Alvarez: One operational question — in the last run we saw tokenization differences between providers causing extra tokens. Any comment?
[06:25] Priya Nandakumar: We use a consistent tokenizer in our tests but providers sometimes differ. We can normalize by running the same tokenization pipeline in-prod or include a token-normalizer in front. We'll include token counts in the next sheet.
[06:38] Marcus Leung: Great. If we proceed with a 7/20 dedicated window, can you guarantee no SLA dips for that week?
[06:45] Jordan Ellis: We'll commit to the SLA for Dedicated, subject to the usual terms. For a short reserved window we also offer an engineer on-call during the test if you want.
[06:54] Ibrahim Conteh: That would be helpful.
[06:57] Jordan Ellis: We'll include that as an option in the follow-up email.
[07:02] Priya Nandakumar: Action item — I'll run the routing test where we toggle prefix cache on/off and quantify p95 improvements and upload artifacts.
[07:10] Sofia Alvarez: I'll send our infra contact for VPC peering and look into the budget.
[07:15] Marcus Leung: I'll confirm the acceptance prompt set and share it with Priya.
[07:20] Jordan Ellis: Great. Any other questions?
[07:24] Sofia Alvarez: One last quick question — how do fallbacks interact with rate limiting? If we route to a cheaper variant and it saturates, do we automatically failover?
[07:32] Priya Nandakumar: Yes we can set a threshold-based fallback: when route error rate or queueing latency breaches X, traffic will divert to the higher-tier route. We also surface those metrics in the console.
[07:43] Marcus Leung: Ok that covers it for me.
[07:47] Jordan Ellis: Thanks everyone — recap in email, I'll attach the raw logs and cost model. Priya will post the routing test results. We'll aim to lock the 7/20 slot by 7/17 if Elytrex confirms.
[07:58] Sofia Alvarez: Thanks all.
[08:00] [call ends]
